newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana Land Q4 volumes, prices up.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana Land Q4 volumes, prices up.

text.p: Louisiana Land and Exploration Co said fourth quarter oil and gas revenues rose 42 percent from 1995's fourth quarter due to increased domestic natural gas volumes and significantly higher commodity prices.

Fourth quarter 1996 domestic natural gas volumes grew 25 percent to 309.5 million cubic feet of natural gas per day (MMCFD), LL&E's highest quarterly domestic gas production rate in over 20 years, LL&E said.
New production in the Gulf of Mexico and south Louisiana accounted for the significant growth in volumes.
North Sea natural gas production volumes averaged 34 MMCFD, up six percent from 32.3 MMCFD in the comparable period last year.
Domestic natural gas prices averaged $2.78 per thousand cubic feet (MCF), up 41 percent from $1.97 per MCF in 1995's fourth quarter, LL&E said.
North Sea gas prices were also greatly improved, averaging $2.61 per MCF, up 32 percent from the same period last year, the company said.
Domestic crude and condensate volumes rose four percent to 21.5 thousand barrels per day (MBPD) from 20.6 MBPD in the fourth quarter of 1995 due to increased production in south Louisiana.
In the North Sea, oil production was initiated at the Thelma Field at T-Block during October of 1996 from the first of four planned wells, the company said.
However, natural declines at the existing T-Block Fields, as well as at LL&E's other North Sea properties more than offset new production at the Thelma Field.
In total, North Sea crude and condensate volumes declined 2.1 MBPD to 15.1 MBPD in 1996's final quarter.

Other foreign crude volumes declined 2.0 MBPD to 3.1 MBPD. Increased production volumes in Colombia from successful development drilling were more than offset by natural declines at the KAKAP concession, offshore Indonesia.
Worldwide crude and condensate prices averaged $22.48 per barrel, up 29 percent from $17.41 in the fourth quarter of the prior year, the company said.

Cash operating costs, which includes lease operating expense, production taxes and general and administrative expenses, were reduced 11 percent to $4.84 per barrel of oil equivalent (BOE) from $5.46 per BOE in the fourth quarter of 1995, the company said.

Dry holes and exploratory charges totaled $37 million in 1996's fourth quarter, up $18.5 million from the same period a year ago, primarily as a result of lease impairments and increased dry hole costs associated with LL&E's expanded exploratory drilling program.
Cash flow from operating activities before changes in working capital items rose 56 percent to $113 million, or $3.27 per share.

Long-term debt stood at $505 million as of December 31, 1996. As a result of the significant reduction in long-term debt over the last twelve months, interest incurred fell 22 percent in the fourth quarter to $10.4 million.
Capital expenditures during the quarter totaled $66 million.

"Our strong fourth quarter results were driven by a 25 percent increase in domestic natural gas deliveries and significantly higher worldwide crude and natural gas prices, LL&E chief executive H. Leighton Steward said.

Also, cash operating costs per barrel were reduced 11 percent. For the full year 1996, net cash flow increased 55 percent to $10.74 per share which enabled us to fully fund a robust exploration program and pay down debt 27 percent," he said.
